The first public version of Oats: a high-signal tool for high-signal conversations.

## Download

- **Apple Silicon** (M1 and later): `Oats-arm64.dmg`
- **Intel**: `Oats-x64.dmg`. It is built for Intel, but nobody has tested it on an Intel Mac yet.

Oats needs macOS 12 Monterey or later.

## The first time you open it

This version is not notarized by Apple yet, so macOS stops it once.

1. Open the DMG and drag Oats to Applications.
2. Open Oats. macOS says that it cannot verify the app. Click Done.
3. Open System Settings, then Privacy & Security. Scroll down and click Open Anyway next to "Oats was blocked".
4. Confirm with your password or Touch ID. macOS asks only once.

## What it does

- Press ⇧⌘O in any app to start or stop. Oats records the conversation in the room with one microphone and transcribes it on your Mac.
- Each question gets a verdict in place: Answered, Unknown, Unanswered or Open.
- New: the context check. Turn it on in Settings and choose a folder of your team's notes. When an answer in the room is unsure, Oats checks it against that folder and your past conversations, and says "That's right" or "Wait, that's wrong", with the passage it used. It uses the writing model you chose.
- Optional, off by default: when the folder has no answer, Oats can ask Claude Code to look in GitHub, Linear and Notion, read-only.
- When you stop: a title, a summary, the threads, talk time per person, and how each question ended.
- Search every transcript, and see all your conversations on one board.

Titles, summaries and the context check need a writing model: a local one that you download in Settings, or your own API key.

## Privacy

Audio and transcripts stay on your Mac. There is no Oats account and no Oats server. Summaries run on a local model, or on your own API key if you add one. When a question meets a clear "I don't know", Oats opens a web search for the question text in your browser. You can turn that off in Settings. The sidebar counts every network request since launch.

Tell people before you record. Some places, for example California, need everyone's consent.

The SHA-256 checksums are in `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
